, while elastic follow-up is a real phenomenon, it is not possible to predict it accurately using a stress range-independent constitutive law.
elastic follow-up is a function of the constitutive law used, with the degree of dependence varying according to the structure and the loading history.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the independence of stress–strain trajectory from the constitutive equation is a characteristic of the elastic follow-up phenomenon, but that this independence is not universal.

the independence of elastic follow-up on constitutive law is not lost with the introduction of a stress range-dependent creep constitutive law but the stress–strain trajectories are different for a stress range-dependent law compared to a simple power law.
the use of a simple constitutive model, based on power-law or Norton-Bailey creep, is adequate for elastic follow-up analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of stress range-dependent constitutions, elastic follow-up cannot be predicted from a stress–strain trajectory.
, in order to use stress–strain trajectories for elastic follow-up estimates, a simple constitutive law must be used.
, for the case of a stress range-dependent law, the use of a simplified method for elastic follow-up is not valid.
